# Grokking Coding Interview

> The 41 coding patterns and how to recognize each one in a new problem. A free guide from DesignGurus.io, in plain Markdown, with no account required.

Each page is short and ends with links to full course lessons and free articles. Each description below is the opening sentence of that page.

## Guide pages

- [Glossary](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/glossary.md): Terms that appear across this repo, in plain language.
- [Resources](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/resources.md): Free reading that goes with this repo, and the paid courses that go deeper.

## Cheat sheets

- [All 41 Patterns, on One Page](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/all-41-patterns.md): The night-before revision sheet.
- [BFS vs DFS: Which Search, and Why](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/bfs-vs-dfs.md): Both visit every node once and both cost O(V + E).
- [Complexity Cheat Sheet](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/complexity-cheat-sheet.md): Every pattern, every data structure, and every common algorithm, with what it costs.
- [Dynamic Programming vs Greedy vs Backtracking](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/dp-vs-greedy-vs-backtracking.md): All three explore a set of choices.
- [Edge Cases Checklist](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/edge-cases-checklist.md): Most failed submissions are not wrong algorithms.
- [Coding Interview Flashcards](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/flashcards.md): 103 question and answer cards over the patterns, the structures, and the traps.
- [How to Talk Through a Coding Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/interview-communication.md): The code is graded, and so is everything around it.
- [Python vs Java vs JavaScript: The Same Twenty Operations](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/python-vs-java-vs-javascript-idioms.md): Knowing the pattern is not enough if you lose four minutes remembering how to build a max-heap.
- [How to Recognize the Pattern in Sixty Seconds](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/recognize-the-pattern.md): You have read a problem you have never seen.
- [What Complexity Passes: Reading the Answer Out of the Constraints](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/what-complexity-passes.md): The size of the input is not decoration.

## Patterns

- [Pattern: 0/1 Knapsack (Dynamic Programming)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/0-1-knapsack.md): You have items, each with a weight and a value, and a bag that can hold a limited weight.
- [Pattern: Articulation Points and Bridges](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/articulation-points-and-bridges.md): In an undirected graph, an articulation point is a vertex whose removal disconnects the graph.
- [Pattern: Backtracking](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/backtracking.md): Backtracking walks a tree of decisions.
- [Pattern: Binary Indexed Tree (Fenwick Tree)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/binary-indexed-tree.md): A binary indexed tree, also called a Fenwick tree, is a flat array where each slot holds the sum of a block of the original array.
- [Pattern: Bitwise XOR](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/bitwise-xor.md): XOR has three properties that do all the work: a ^ a = 0, a ^ 0 = a, and the order of operations does not matter.
- [Pattern: Clone](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/clone.md): A deep copy means the new structure shares no nodes with the old one, so changing the copy leaves the original untouched.
- [Pattern: Counting](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/counting.md): A large family of problems reduces to one frequency table plus a little logic on top of it.
- [Pattern: Cyclic Sort](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/cyclic-sort.md): Normal sorting compares elements against each other, and no comparison sort can beat O(n log n).
- [Pattern: Fast and Slow Pointers](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/fast-and-slow-pointers.md): One pointer takes one step at a time.
- [Pattern: Fibonacci Numbers (Dynamic Programming)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/fibonacci-numbers.md): The Fibonacci recurrence, f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2), is the simplest shape in dynamic programming.
- [Pattern: Graphs](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/graphs.md): A graph is a set of nodes and the connections between them.
- [Pattern: Greedy Algorithms](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/greedy-algorithms.md): A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step and never reconsiders it.
- [Pattern: Hash Maps](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/hash-maps.md): A hash map stores key to value pairs and looks them up in constant time on average.
- [Pattern: In-place Reversal of a Linked List](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/in-place-reversal-of-a-linked-list.md): Reversing a linked list by building a new one is easy and costs O(n) memory.
- [Pattern: Island (Matrix Traversal)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/island-matrix-traversal.md): In a grid problem, each cell is a node and its adjacent cells are its edges.
- [Pattern: K-way Merge](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/k-way-merge.md): Merging two sorted lists is easy with two pointers: compare the two heads and take the smaller one.
- [Pattern: Linear Sorting Algorithms](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/linear-sorting-algorithms.md): Comparison sorts have a proven lower bound of O(n log n), because there are n!
- [Pattern: Meet in the Middle](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/meet-in-the-middle.md): Some problems have no better answer than trying every subset, and 2^40 is far too many.
- [Pattern: Merge Intervals](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/merge-intervals.md): An interval is a pair of numbers, a start and an end.
- [Pattern: Modified Binary Search](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/modified-binary-search.md): The textbook version searches a sorted array for a value.
- [Pattern: Monotonic Queue](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/monotonic-queue.md): A monotonic stack can only be touched at one end.
- [Pattern: Monotonic Stack](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/monotonic-stack.md): A monotonic stack is a stack whose values are kept in order, either always increasing or always decreasing from bottom to top.
- [Pattern: Mo's Algorithm](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/mos-algorithm.md): You are given a fixed array and many queries of the form "tell me something about the range from L to R".
- [Pattern: Multi-threaded](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/multi-threaded.md): In a concurrency question, the code itself is usually short.
- [Pattern: Ordered Set](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/ordered-set.md): An ordered set keeps its elements sorted at all times, usually with a balanced binary search tree.
- [Pattern: Palindromic Subsequence (Dynamic Programming)](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/palindromic-subsequence.md): Most one-dimensional dynamic programming asks "what is the best answer ending at position i".
- [Pattern: Prefix Sum](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/prefix-sum.md): A prefix sum array holds, at each position, the total of everything up to that point.
- [Pattern: Segment Tree](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/segment-tree.md): Prefix sums answer range queries in O(1), but only while the array never changes.
- [Pattern: Serialize and Deserialize](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/serialize-and-deserialize.md): Serializing a tree means writing it out as text.
- [Pattern: Simulation](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/simulation.md): A simulation problem describes a process, and the answer is whatever the process produces.
- [Pattern: Sliding Window](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/sliding-window.md): A window is a contiguous stretch of the array or string, marked by a left and a right index.
- [Pattern: Stacks](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/stacks.md): A stack stores items in last-in, first-out order.
- [Pattern: Subsets](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/subsets.md): There are 2^n subsets of a set of n elements, because each element is either in or out.
- [Pattern: Top K Elements](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/top-k-elements.md): If you only need the K largest values, sorting all n of them does far more work than the question asked for.
- [Pattern: Topological Sort](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/topological-sort.md): Given tasks with prerequisites, a topological order is any sequence where each task appears after everything it depends on.
- [Pattern: Tree Depth First Search](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/tree-depth-first-search.md): Depth first search on a tree means: solve the left subtree, solve the right subtree, then combine the two answers at the current node.
- [Pattern: Tree Level Order Traversal](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/tree-level-order-traversal.md): Level order traversal, also called breadth first search on a tree, uses a queue.
- [Pattern: Trie](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/trie.md): A trie, also called a prefix tree, holds a set of strings.
- [Pattern: Two Heaps](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/two-heaps.md): A heap gives you the smallest or the largest element instantly, but nothing about the middle.
- [Pattern: Two Pointers](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/two-pointers.md): Two Pointers keeps two positions in the same array or string and moves them under a rule.
- [Pattern: Union Find](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/patterns/union-find.md): Union Find, also called a disjoint set union, maintains a collection of groups.

## Problems

- [Balanced Parentheses](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/balanced-parentheses.md): You are given a string of brackets, which may mix round, square, and curly.
- [Binary Tree Level Order Traversal](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/binary-tree-level-order-traversal.md): You are given the root of a binary tree.
- [Clone Graph](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/clone-graph.md): You are given a reference to a node in a connected undirected graph.
- [Container With Most Water](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/container-with-most-water.md): You are given an array where each entry is the height of a vertical line, and the lines stand one unit apart.
- [Daily Temperatures](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/daily-temperatures.md): You are given an array of daily temperatures.
- [Find the Median of a Number Stream](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/find-the-median-of-a-number-stream.md): Design a structure with two operations.
- [Find the Missing Number](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/find-the-missing-number.md): You are given an array of n distinct numbers, all drawn from the range 0 to n.
- [LinkedList Cycle](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/linkedlist-cycle.md): You are given the head of a singly linked list.
- [Merge Intervals](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/merge-intervals.md): You are given a list of intervals, each a start and an end.
- [Merge K Sorted Lists](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/merge-k-sorted-lists.md): You are given K linked lists, each already sorted in ascending order.
- [Minimum Meeting Rooms](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/minimum-meeting-rooms.md): You are given meetings, each with a start and an end time.
- [Number of Islands](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/number-of-islands.md): You are given a 2D grid where each cell is land or water.
- [Reverse a LinkedList](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/reverse-a-linked-list.md): You are given the head of a singly linked list.
- [Search in Rotated Array](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/search-in-rotated-array.md): You are given an array that was sorted in ascending order and then rotated at some unknown pivot, so [1,2,3,4,5] might arrive as [4,5,1,2,3].
- [Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.md): Design two functions.
- [Smallest Window containing Substring](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/smallest-window-containing-substring.md): You are given a string and a pattern.
- [Subarray Sum Equals K](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/subarray-sum-equals-k.md): You are given an array of integers and a target k.
- [Subsets](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/subsets.md): You are given a list of distinct integers.
- [Tasks Scheduling](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/tasks-scheduling.md): You are given a number of tasks and a list of prerequisite pairs.
- [Two Sum](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/two-sum.md): You are given an array of integers and a target number.
- [Validate Binary Search Tree](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/validate-binary-search-tree.md): You are given the root of a binary tree.
- [Word Search](https://github.com/design-gurus/grokking-coding-interview/blob/main/problems/word-search.md): You are given a grid of letters and a word.
